entries.why_wrong: The `continue` in `default` doesn't skip any tickets — it just moves on to the next loop iteration, which is exactly what you want for non-urgent tickets. The real problem is on the other side of the switch: once a match is found, `break` only exits the switch, not the for loop, so scanning continues and later urgent tickets overwrite the earlier result.

`i < tickets.length` is the correct bound here; changing it to `<=` would make the loop read past the end of the array and access `undefined`. The actual bug has nothing to do with the loop's range — it's that `break` inside the `'urgent'` case only exits the switch, so the loop keeps running after a match and lets a later urgent ticket overwrite `result`.

`result` is initialized right away with `let result = null`, so there's no ReferenceError — it's always defined by the time the loop runs. The bug is instead that the `break` inside the `'urgent'` case only exits the switch statement, so the loop doesn't stop at the first match and later urgent tickets keep overwriting `result`.

`switch` already compares with strict equality under the hood, so there's no type coercion happening between `tickets[i].priority` and `'urgent'` to fix here. The actual defect is that `break` in the `'urgent'` case only exits the switch, not the surrounding for loop, so scanning continues and the last urgent ticket ends up overwriting the first.
